name: Immunotactoid or Fibrillary Glomerulopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunofluorescence Diagnostic Criteria for Immunotactoid and Fibrillary Glomerulopathy

criteria.description: Identification of organized microtubular or fibrillary deposits in glomeruli by electron microscopy
Positive immunofluorescence staining for immunoglobulins and complement components in glomerular deposits
Presence of proteinuria and/or nephrotic syndrome with or without renal insufficiency
Exclusion of other causes of organized glomerular deposits such as amyloidosis and cryoglobulinemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic organized deposits on electron microscopy combined with positive immunofluorescence and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires renal biopsy with electron microscopy and immunofluorescence studies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electron microscopy revealing microtubular or fibrillary glomerular deposits
pathognomonic.notes: Distinct ultrastructural pattern differentiates from other glomerulopathies
searchTerms: kidney deposits seen on electron microscope
tiny fibers or tubes in kidney filter

common.notes: Mild to moderate elevation in blood pressure
Presence of red blood cells in urine sediment

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

occasional.notes: Rarely reported in association with paraproteinemia
Mild joint pain without inflammatory arthritis

rare.notes: May occur in cases with overlapping features
Extremely rare complication in renal impairment
searchTerms: skin thickening and hardening due to kidney disease
fibrotic skin changes from kidney failure
systemic skin fibrosis related to kidney problems

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Positive immunofluorescence for IgG, C3 in glomeruli
imaging: Electron microscopy showing organized microtubular or fibrillary deposits (10-30 nm diameter fibrils or microtubules)
other: Renal biopsy showing mesangial expansion and capillary wall thickening
Exclusion of amyloid by Congo red staining

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrils 8-12 nm in diameter on electron microscopy
Immune complex deposits with different ultrastructure
Immune complex deposits without organized fibrils

redFlags: Nephrotic syndrome refractory to standard therapy
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting paraproteinemia or vasculitis
references: Nasr SH, et al. Immunotactoid glomerulopathy: clinicopathologic study of 73 cases. Kidney Int. 2019.
Fogo AB. Fibrillary glomerulonephritis: a review. Kidney Int. 2015.
